note: Known deficit for tools/release/check_production_stream_defaults.py: 27 sites across 8 production files. Every entry is a production function or member that defaults its cudaStream_t to nullptr, which in a codebase whose compute and load streams are created with cudaStreamNonBlocking is a write whose ordering against the kernels that read it is unspecified. docs/research/kv-publish-stream-ordering.md records the mechanism and why the fix is not being applied speculatively. Tests are excluded on purpose: a defaulted stream in a test is correct, because nothing there races a compute stream. The count is by any parameter name, not only one called `stream` -- an earlier survey that matched only the name `stream` reported 32 and missed device.h's transfer_stream, device.cu's compute and load, and device.h's stream_. This pin is a ratchet, not a detector: it fails on ANY difference, so a count that grows is a regression and a count that shrinks is the upstream fix arriving and needing a deliberate, recorded update. Editing this file is the record of that decision. Updated 2026-09-29: upstream 064965c7 (refactor(kv): require explicit publication streams) removed the nullptr defaults from kv_store.h (5 sites) and paged_kv_cache.h (3 of 7), reducing the total from 36 to 28. Updated 2026-10-01: the FP8 TMA descriptor is now passed by value at alignas(64) on every platform, which deleted Fp8TmaDescriptorBlock entirely -- that struct held the file's only defaulted cudaStream_t (stream = nullptr), so the site is gone rather than moved. 28 to 27.
